questions.question: Which of the following articles of Indian Constitution is related to the Election Commission of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 324**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 324** of the Indian Constitution deals with the powers, functions, tenure, eligibility, etc., of the Election Commission of India.
 
• It provides that the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of the electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to Parliament and to the Legislature of every State and of elections to the offices of President and Vice-President held under this Constitution shall be vested in a Commission (referred to in this Constitution as the Election Commission).
 
• The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
 
• The body administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies in India, and the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India**

 
 
• The Election Commission of India was established in accordance with the Constitution on 25th January 1950.
 
• The commission has the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President in India.
 
• It is a permanent and independent body to ensure free and fair elections in the country.
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners are appointed by the President of India. They have a tenure of six years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Articles Related to Elections in India**
 
 
• **Article 324** - Superintendence, direction, and control of elections to be vested in an Election Commission.
 
• **Article 325** - No person to be ineligible for inclusion in or to claim to be included in a special, electoral roll on grounds of religion, race, caste, or sex.
 
• **Article 326** - Elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assemblies of States to be on the basis of adult suffrage.
 
• **Article 327** - Power of Parliament to make provision with respect to elections to Legislatures.
 
• **Article 328** - Power of Legislature of a State to make provision with respect to elections to such Legislature.

questions.question:
Read the following about the Green Revolution in India.

A. The green revolution in India refers to a period when Indian Agriculture was converted into an industrial system due to the adoption of modern methods and technology such as the use of HYV seeds, tractors, irrigation facilities, pesticides and fertilizers.

B. It was funded by the US and the Indian Government and the Ford and Rockefeller Foundation.

Identify the CORRECT statement/statements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India marks a period of significant agricultural transformation in the country.
 
• This transformation was characterized by the adoption of new technologies, including High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, tractors, irrigation facilities, pesticides, and fertilizers.
 
• The revolution aimed at increasing agricultural productivity to make India self-sufficient in food grains.
 
• The initiative was financially supported by the Indian government, the United States, and international organizations such as the Ford and Rockefeller Foundations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High Yielding Variety (HYV) Seeds**

 
 
• HYV seeds are a type of seed that has been specifically bred to produce more crops per acre compared to traditional seeds.
 
• They were a key component of the Green Revolution and helped significantly increase agricultural production.
 
 
 
• **Tractors and Mechanization**
 
 
• The use of tractors and other machinery helped speed up farming processes and reduce the need for manual labor.
 
• This mechanization was crucial in transforming Indian agriculture into an industrial system.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation Facilities**
 
 
• The development and expansion of irrigation facilities ensured a more reliable water supply for crops, which is essential for high agricultural productivity.
 
• Improved irrigation helped mitigate the effects of drought and other water-related issues.
 
 
 
• **Pesticides and Fertilizers**
 
 
• The use of chemical pesticides and fertilizers helped protect crops from pests and diseases, and provided essential nutrients to the soil.
 
• These inputs were critical in achieving the high yields associated with the Green Revolution.
 
 
 
• **Ford and Rockefeller Foundations**
 
 
• These foundations played a significant role in providing financial and technical support for the Green Revolution.
 
• They helped fund research and development of new agricultural technologies and practices.

questions.question: The Green Revolution in India primarily focused on improving the production of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**wheat and rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India was initiated in the 1960s and it primarily focused on improving the agricultural production of major food grains, especially wheat and rice.
 
• This revolution led to the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, particularly for wheat and rice, which significantly boosted the production and yield per hectare.
 
• The initiative was largely funded and supported by various international organizations, including the Rockefeller Foundation and the Ford Foundation.
 
• Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is considered as the father of the Green Revolution in India for his pivotal role in the development and introduction of these high-yielding variety seeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that occurred between the 1940s and the late 1960s, which increased agricultural production worldwide, particularly in developing countries.
 
• It involved the development and dissemination of new seed varieties, the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, and the implementation of new agricultural practices such as irrigation and mechanization.
 
• The primary goal was to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains and to combat hunger and malnutrition.
 
• Despite its success in increasing food production, the Green Revolution also led to environmental and social issues, such as soil degradation, water scarcity, and increased inequality among farmers.
 
 
 
• **High-Yielding Variety (HYV) Seeds:**
 
 
• HYV seeds are a type of seed that has been bred to produce more yield per acre than traditional varieties.
 
• These seeds are often resistant to certain diseases and pests, and they respond well to fertilizers and irrigation.
 
• The use of HYV seeds was a key component of the Green Revolution, significantly increasing the production of staple crops like wheat and rice.
 
• However, HYV seeds often require more inputs (such as water and fertilizers) and can lead to monoculture practices, which may reduce biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Dr. M.S. Swaminathan:**
 
 
• Dr. Monkombu Sambasivan Swaminathan is an Indian geneticist and international administrator, renowned for his leading role in India's Green Revolution.
 
• He is known as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India" for his work in the development of high-yielding variety seeds.
 
• Dr. Swaminathan's efforts led to significant increases in food grain production in India, helping to alleviate hunger and improve food security in the country.
 
• He has received numerous awards and honors for his contributions to agriculture and food security, including the Padma Bhushan and the Padma Vibhushan.

questions.question: Gopika Varma receives the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2018 for her contribution to _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohiniyattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gopika Varma** is a renowned exponent of the classical dance form, Mohiniyattam.
 
• She has contributed significantly to the **revival and popularization** of Mohiniyattam.
 
• Gopika Varma has received numerous awards for her contributions, including the prestigious **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in 2018.
 
• Mohiniyattam is characterized by its **graceful movements and gentle, swaying body motions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohiniyattam**

 
 
• Mohiniyattam is one of the **eight classical dances of India**, originating from Kerala.
 
• The name Mohiniyattam comes from "Mohini", a divine enchantress avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu, and "attam", meaning dance.
 
• It is known for its **graceful and delicate** nature, with movements that are soft and lyrical.
 
• The dance form typically includes themes of **love and devotion**, often narrating stories from Hindu mythology.
 
 
 
• **Kathak**
 
 
• Kathak is another classical dance form of India, originating from the northern part of the country.
 
• It is known for its intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures and is often performed as a storytelling dance.
 
• Kathak has three main gharanas (schools): Jaipur, Lucknow, and Banaras.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**
 
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical Indian dance form that originated in the state of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is known for its fast rhythms and fluid movements, along with dramatic characterization.
 
• Kuchipudi typically includes both pure dance and expressive dance segments.
 
 
 
• **Odissi**
 
 
• Odissi is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha.
 
• It is characterized by its sculptural poses, fluid movements, and strong footwork.
 
• Odissi dance often depicts themes related to Lord Jagannath and other spiritual narratives.

questions.question: Who is the first Indian singer to have perform at the Royal Albert Hall in London?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lata Mangeshkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lata Mangeshkar** is one of the most revered and celebrated playback singers in India.
 
• She performed at the **Royal Albert Hall** in London in 1974, making her the first Indian singer to achieve this feat.
 
• The Royal Albert Hall is one of the most prestigious concert halls in the world, known for hosting a variety of high-profile events and performances.
 
• Lata Mangeshkar's performance at the Royal Albert Hall is a testament to her international acclaim and the global recognition of her talent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lata Mangeshkar**

 
 
• Born on September 28, 1929, in Indore, India, Lata Mangeshkar is widely regarded as one of the greatest and most influential vocalists in the history of Indian music.
 
• She has recorded songs in over a thousand Hindi films and has sung songs in over thirty-six regional Indian languages and foreign languages.
 
• Her career spans over seven decades, and she has received numerous awards, including the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award.
 
• Lata Mangeshkar is often referred to as the "Nightingale of India" due to her melodious voice and significant contributions to Indian music.
 
 
 
• **Royal Albert Hall**
 
 
• Located in London, the Royal Albert Hall is a concert hall that was opened in 1871 by Queen Victoria in memory of her husband, Prince Albert.
 
• The hall is known for its distinctive architecture and has a seating capacity of approximately 5,272 people.
 
• It hosts a wide range of events, including classical concerts, rock and pop performances, ballet, opera, and charity events.
 
• The Royal Albert Hall has been associated with many notable performers and events, making it a symbol of cultural and musical heritage.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Indian Singers**
 
 
• **K. J. Yesudas**: An acclaimed Indian playback singer and classical musician known for his work in South Indian cinema.
 
• **Asha Bhosle**: A versatile playback singer who has recorded thousands of songs in various Indian and foreign languages.
 
• **A.R Rahman**: A renowned composer and singer known for his work in Indian cinema and international projects, including winning Oscars for his work on the film "Slumdog Millionaire".

questions.question: Who became the first Indian to receive the Grand Order of the Chain of Yellow Star in the republic of Suriname in June, 2023?

• Droupadi Murmu is an Indian politician who has served as the President of India since July 2022.
 
• She became the first tribal woman to hold the position of President in India.
 
• In June 2023, she was awarded the Grand Order of the Chain of Yellow Star, a prestigious honor from the Republic of Suriname.
 
• This award recognizes her contributions to the upliftment of marginalized communities and her efforts in promoting social justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grand Order of the Chain of Yellow Star**

 
 
• This is one of the highest civilian honors awarded by the Republic of Suriname.
 
• The award is given to individuals who have made significant contributions to the betterment of society and international relations.
 
• Recipients of this prestigious award have demonstrated exemplary service in their respective fields, contributing to global peace and cooperation.
 
 
 
• **Republic of Suriname**
 
 
• Suriname is a country located on the northeastern Atlantic coast of South America.
 
• It is bordered by the Atlantic Ocean to the north, French Guiana to the east, Guyana to the west, and Brazil to the south.
 
• Suriname's capital and largest city is Paramaribo.
 
• The country has a diverse culture with influences from various ethnic groups including East Indians, Africans, Indonesians, Chinese, and Europeans.
 
 
 
• **Droupadi Murmu's Contributions**

• She has been actively involved in social work, particularly in the areas of education and women’s rights.

questions.question: To which of the following states does the dance form Laho belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The dance form Laho is an important part of the traditional culture of Meghalaya.
 
• It is performed during the festival of Shad Suk Mynsiem, which is celebrated by the Khasi tribe of Meghalaya.
 
• Laho dance involves both men and women dancing together, usually in a circular formation, with rhythmic steps and movements.
 
• It is a joyous and vibrant dance that showcases the rich cultural heritage of the Khasi tribe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meghalaya**

 
 
• Meghalaya is a state in northeastern India. It was formed by carving out two districts from the state of Assam in 1972.
 
• The name "Meghalaya" means "the abode of clouds" in Sanskrit.
 
• It is known for its rich cultural heritage, with a majority of the population belonging to the Khasi, Garo, and Jaintia tribes.
 
• Meghalaya is famous for its breathtaking landscapes, dense forests, and abundant rainfall. Cherrapunji and Mawsynram, located in Meghalaya, are among the wettest places on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Laho Dance**
 
 
• Laho is a traditional dance of the Khasi tribe in Meghalaya.
 
• It is performed during festivals and community gatherings, especially during the spring festival of Shad Suk Mynsiem.
 
• The dance involves alternating male and female dancers, who hold hands and move rhythmically to the beat of traditional drums and music.
 
• Laho is not just a dance but also a social event where the community comes together to celebrate and strengthen their cultural bonds.
 
 
 
• **Shad Suk Mynsiem**
 
 
• Shad Suk Mynsiem, also known as the "Dance of the Joyful Heart," is a major festival of the Khasi tribe in Meghalaya.
 
• It is celebrated in April, marking the beginning of the agricultural season.
 
• The festival features traditional dances, music, and rituals that express gratitude to the gods for a bountiful harvest and seek blessings for the upcoming season.
 
• The Laho dance is a prominent feature of this festival, symbolizing joy and unity among the community.

questions.question: Which state's government has granted approval for the 'Location Accessible Multi-modal Initiative (LACCMI)' scheme, aimed at establishing a sustainable, affordable, and safe transportation network for passengers and goods across the state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The government of Odisha has granted approval for the 'Location Accessible Multi-modal Initiative (LACCMI)' scheme.
 
• The LACCMI scheme aims to establish a sustainable, affordable, and safe transportation network.
 
• This initiative is designed to cater to the needs of both passengers and goods across the state.
 
• The scheme is part of Odisha's efforts to enhance its transportation infrastructure and connectivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sustainable Transportation**

 
 
• Sustainable transportation refers to the provision of services and infrastructure for the mobility of people and goods in a manner that is safe, affordable, and environmentally friendly.
 
• It aims to reduce the negative impacts of transportation on the environment and human health.
 
• Sustainable transportation includes the development of public transportation systems, promotion of non-motorized transport, and the use of cleaner energy sources.
 
 
 
• **Affordable Transportation**
 
 
• Affordable transportation ensures that transportation costs are within the means of the general population.
 
• It focuses on reducing the financial burden on individuals and families, especially those from low-income groups.
 
• Affordable transportation can include subsidies, fare reductions, and the provision of low-cost alternatives.
 
 
 
• **Safe Transportation**
 
 
• Safe transportation ensures the safety and security of passengers and goods during transit.
 
• It involves implementing measures to prevent accidents, injuries, and crimes.
 
• Safety measures can include the use of modern technology, strict regulations, and continuous monitoring.
 
 
 
• **Multi-modal Transportation**
 
 
• Multi-modal transportation refers to the use of two or more modes of transportation to move people or goods.
 
• This approach aims to provide efficient and seamless connectivity across different transportation networks.
 
• Examples of multi-modal transportation include integrating bus, train, and ferry services, as well as combining road, rail, and air transportation for freight.

questions.question: In September 2023, Vijayawada Railway Station was awarded the _______ -certification with the highest rating of Platinum by the Indian Green Building Council (IGBC).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Green Railway Station**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vijayawada Railway Station was awarded the Green Railway Station certification by the Indian Green Building Council (IGBC).
 
• The certification was given in September 2023, recognizing the station's sustainable practices and eco-friendly infrastructure.
 
• It achieved the highest rating of Platinum, indicating excellence in green building standards.
 
• This recognition is part of the IGBC's efforts to promote environmentally sustainable construction and operation in the railway sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Green Building Council (IGBC)**

 
 
• It is a part of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) and was formed in 2001.
 
• IGBC is responsible for promoting green building concepts in India, providing certifications for sustainable buildings.
 
• Green building certification by IGBC includes various ratings such as Certified, Silver, Gold, and Platinum based on the level of sustainability achieved.

• This includes energy-efficient lighting, water conservation measures, waste management systems, and the use of renewable energy sources.
 
• Such stations aim to provide a healthier environment for passengers and staff while reducing the carbon footprint.

questions.question: When a person leaves one job (either voluntarily or involuntarily) without finding another one, they are known to be going through _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frictional unemployment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Frictional unemployment** occurs when individuals are temporarily unemployed while transitioning from one job to another.
 
• This type of unemployment is often voluntary as individuals may leave their jobs to find better opportunities or due to personal reasons.
 
• Frictional unemployment is considered a natural part of a healthy economy as it indicates that workers have the flexibility to find jobs that better match their skills and interests.
 
• This type of unemployment is usually short-term and does not indicate a fundamental problem in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disguised unemployment:**

 
 
• This occurs when more people are employed than actually needed. In other words, some workers have zero or marginal productivity.
 
• It is common in agricultural sectors where family members may work on the same plot of land but not all of them are necessary for the production output.
 
• It does not affect the overall production output and is often a characteristic of developing economies.
 
 
 
• **Cyclical unemployment:**
 
 
• This type of unemployment is related to the cyclical trends in the economy, such as the fluctuations of the business cycle.
 
• During periods of economic downturns or recessions, demand for goods and services decreases, leading to job losses.
 
• Cyclical unemployment is usually temporary and can be addressed through economic policies that stimulate demand.
 
 
 
• **Seasonal unemployment:**
 
 
• This type of unemployment occurs at certain times of the year when demand for labor in certain industries is low.
 
• It is common in industries like agriculture, tourism, and construction, where activities are dependent on seasons.
 
• Workers in these industries may be unemployed during off-seasons but find employment during peak seasons.

questions.question: Major Dhyan Chand is a famous name in the game of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hockey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Major Dhyan Chand is widely regarded as one of the greatest field hockey players of all time.
 
• He was part of the Indian hockey team that won three Olympic gold medals in 1928, 1932, and 1936.
 
• His extraordinary goal-scoring ability earned him the nickname "The Wizard" or "The Magician" of hockey.
 
• Major Dhyan Chand's birthday, August 29, is celebrated as National Sports Day in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Field Hockey**

 
 
• Field hockey is a team sport played on grass or artificial turf, where teams use curved sticks to hit a small, hard ball into the opposing team's goal.
 
• It is an Olympic sport, with men’s field hockey being included since 1908 and women’s field hockey since 1980.
 
• The game is known for its fast pace, requiring skillful dribbling, passing, and strategic play.
 
• Field hockey is popular in many countries, particularly in Europe, Asia, Australia, and Africa.
 
 
 
• **Olympic Games**
 
 
• The Olympic Games are a major international multi-sport event divided into summer and winter editions, with athletes from around the world competing.
 
• Field hockey has been a part of the Summer Olympics program since 1908 for men and since 1980 for women.
 
• Winning an Olympic medal is considered one of the highest achievements in the sport.
 
• India is historically one of the most successful nations in Olympic field hockey, especially during the early to mid-20th century.
 
 
 
• **National Sports Day**
 
 
• India celebrates National Sports Day on August 29 every year to honor the legendary hockey player Major Dhyan Chand.
 
• On this day, various sports events and activities are organized across the country to promote sports and physical fitness.
 
• The President of India gives out sports-related awards like the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, Arjuna Award, Dronacharya Award, and Dhyan Chand Award on this occasion.
 
• It serves as a reminder of the importance of sports in maintaining health, discipline, and teamwork.

questions.question: Which of the following festival is celebrated on 25th December all over the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Christmas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Christmas is celebrated on 25th December each year to commemorate the birth of Jesus Christ, who is the central figure of Christianity.
 
• This festival is marked by various traditions such as exchanging gifts, decorating Christmas trees, and attending church services.
 
• Christmas is observed as a public holiday in many countries around the world, making it one of the most widely celebrated holidays globally.
 
• Santa Claus, also known as Father Christmas, is a popular figure associated with Christmas, believed to bring gifts to well-behaved children on Christmas Eve.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eid**

 
 
• Eid is a significant Islamic festival celebrated by Muslims worldwide.
 
• There are two major Eids in the Islamic calendar: Eid al-Fitr, which marks the end of Ramadan, and Eid al-Adha, which commemorates the willingness of Ibrahim (Abraham) to sacrifice his son as an act of obedience to God.
 
• Both festivals involve communal prayers, feasting, and giving charity to the less fortunate.
 
 
 
• **Diwali**
 
 
• Diwali, also known as the Festival of Lights, is one of the most popular Hindu festivals.
 
• It symbolizes the victory of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance.
 
• People celebrate Diwali by lighting oil lamps, bursting fireworks, and sharing sweets with family and friends.
 
 
 
• **Holi**
 
 
• Holi, known as the Festival of Colors, is a vibrant Hindu festival celebrated in spring.
 
• It signifies the arrival of spring, the end of winter, and the blossoming of love.
 
• Holi is celebrated by throwing colored powders and water at each other, dancing, and enjoying festive foods.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT associated with musical instrument Sarangi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nikhil Banerjee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ustad Bindadin Khan** was a renowned Sarangi player who made significant contributions to the instrument.
 
• **Ramesh Mishra** is another prominent Sarangi player known for his exceptional skill and performances.
 
• **Shakoor Khan** was also associated with the Sarangi and contributed to its prominence in Indian classical music.
 
• Nikhil Banerjee, however, was a famous **sitar player** and not associated with the Sarangi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarangi**:

 
 
• The Sarangi is a bowed, short-necked string instrument from the Indian subcontinent, used in Hindustani classical music.
 
• It is known for its deep, resonant sound and is considered one of the most difficult instruments to master.
 
• The Sarangi is traditionally made from a block of red cedar wood and has three main playing strings and a series of sympathetic strings.
 
• The instrument is played with a bow, and the player's fingers press the strings directly on the neck without the use of a fingerboard.
 
 
 
• **Nikhil Banerjee**:
 
 
• Nikhil Banerjee was a distinguished Indian sitar player, known for his virtuosity and deep musical insight.
 
• He was a disciple of Ustad Allauddin Khan, the founder of the Maihar Gharana.
 
• Banerjee's playing style was characterized by its lyrical quality and the depth of his ragas.
 
• He received numerous accolades for his contributions to Indian classical music, including the Padma Bhushan in 1976.

questions.question: Which one is not the festival of Gujarat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sunburn Festival**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sunburn Festival is an electronic dance music festival held in India.
 
• It is primarily associated with the state of Goa, where it was first held in 2007.
 
• Sunburn has grown to become one of Asia's largest music festivals.
 
• It attracts international artists and a large audience from around the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uttarayan Kite Festival**

 
 
• Uttarayan, also known as the International Kite Festival, is celebrated every year in Gujarat.
 
• It marks the day when winter begins to turn into summer, according to the Indian calendar.
 
• People celebrate by flying kites and organizing kite competitions.
 
• The festival is particularly famous in the city of Ahmedabad.
 
 
 
• **Kutch Festival**
 
 
• The Kutch Festival, also known as Rann Utsav, is a cultural festival held in the Kutch region of Gujarat.
 
• It showcases the art, music, dance, crafts, and cuisine of the region.
 
• The festival usually takes place in the winter months from November to February.
 
• Tourists can enjoy the vibrant cultural activities and the picturesque white desert of the Rann of Kutch.
 
 
 
• **Paragliding Festival**
 
 
• The Paragliding Festival in Gujarat is an adventure sports event.
 
• It is usually organized in the Saputara region, known for its hilly terrain.
 
• The festival aims to promote tourism and adventure sports in the state.
 
• Enthusiasts from various parts of the country participate in paragliding and other adventure activities.

questions.question: The ______ literacy rates exclude Assam where the Census could not be conducted.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1981**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 1981 Census of India could not be conducted in Assam due to the prevailing law and order situation at that time.
 
• As a result, literacy rates for the 1981 Census exclude the state of Assam.
 
• This exclusion was a significant event in the history of Indian census operations, marking one of the few instances where a state was not included in the national census.
 
• The data for literacy rates was calculated for the rest of India while excluding Assam for that particular census year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census of India**

 
 
• The Census of India is a comprehensive exercise that is conducted every ten years to collect demographic, social, and economic information about the population of India.
 
• It is the largest administrative exercise of its kind in the world, managed by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The first Census of India was conducted in 1872, but the first synchronous census was conducted in 1881.
 
• The data collected through the census is critical for policy-making, planning, and administration at various levels of government.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate**
 
 
• Literacy rate refers to the percentage of people who are able to read and write with understanding in a particular age group, usually 7 years and above.
 
• It is an important indicator of human development and social progress.
 
• Higher literacy rates are associated with better socio-economic outcomes, including improved health, higher income levels, and greater political participation.
 
• In India, literacy rates are measured during the decennial census and are used to assess the effectiveness of educational policies and programs.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Conducting Census**
 
 
• Conducting a census in a large and diverse country like India poses numerous challenges, including logistical issues, security concerns, and ensuring accuracy.
 
• Factors such as political unrest, natural disasters, and difficult terrain can hinder the census process.
 
• Special efforts are made to ensure the inclusion of marginalized and remote communities.
 
• Technological advancements and the use of digital tools have been introduced to improve the efficiency and accuracy of census operations.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of 1981 Census**
 
 
• The 1981 Census is notable for the exclusion of Assam due to the Assam Movement, which was a mass agitation against illegal immigration and demand for the identification and deportation of illegal immigrants.
 
• The movement led to widespread violence and disruption, making it impossible to conduct the census in the state.
 
• As a result, the data for Assam was collected separately in the subsequent census years.
 
• This event highlighted the impact of socio-political conditions on large-scale administrative exercises like the census.

questions.question: The Modern Periodic Table has 18 vertical columns known as 'groups' and _______ horizontal rows known as 'periods'.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Modern Periodic Table is arranged in 7 horizontal rows called periods.
 
• Each period corresponds to the number of electron shells in the atoms of the elements in that row.
 
• The periods are numbered from 1 to 7, starting from the top to the bottom of the table.
 
• The length of each period increases as you move down the periodic table because higher periods contain more elements due to the increase in the number of available orbitals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Groups:**

 
 
• There are 18 vertical columns in the Modern Periodic Table known as groups.
 
• Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties and the same number of valence electrons.
 
• Groups are numbered from 1 to 18, starting from the leftmost column to the rightmost column of the table.
 
• Examples include Group 1 (Alkali metals), Group 2 (Alkaline earth metals), Group 17 (Halogens), and Group 18 (Noble gases).
 
 
 
• **Periods:**
 
 
• The horizontal rows in the periodic table are called periods.
 
• Each period indicates the principal energy level that is being filled with electrons.
 
• Period 1 has 2 elements (Hydrogen and Helium), Periods 2 and 3 have 8 elements each, Periods 4 and 5 have 18 elements each, and Periods 6 and 7 have 32 elements each.
 
• The properties of elements gradually change as you move across a period from left to right.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Law:**
 
 
• The Modern Periodic Table is based on the periodic law, which states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.
 
• This means that elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number, and elements with similar properties recur at regular intervals.
 
 
 
• **Electron Configuration:**
 
 
• Electron configuration refers to the distribution of electrons in the orbitals of an atom.
 
• It follows the Aufbau principle, Hund's rule, and the Pauli exclusion principle.
 
• The electron configuration of an element determines its position in the periodic table and its chemical behavior.

questions.question:
Which of the following events was played in National Games 2023?

I. Rowing

II. Rollball
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Games 2023 included a variety of sports to promote athletic talent across the country.
 
• Rowing is a traditional sport that involves racing boats using oars and has been a part of many national and international competitions.
 
• Rollball is a relatively new sport that combines elements of roller skating and basketball and is gaining popularity in India.
 
• The inclusion of both Rowing and Rollball in the National Games 2023 highlights the diversity and inclusivity of the event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rowing**

 
 
• Rowing is one of the oldest Olympic sports and requires a high level of endurance, strength, and coordination.
 
• It involves racing boats on water, either in sculling (each rower has two oars) or sweep rowing (each rower has one oar).
 
• Rowing events can be held over various distances, commonly 2000 meters in major competitions.
 
• Rowing is governed by the International Rowing Federation (FISA) globally and by the Rowing Federation of India (RFI) in India.
 
 
 
• **Rollball**
 
 
• Rollball is a team sport played on roller skates, combining elements of basketball, handball, and throwball.
 
• The game is played between two teams of six players each, where the objective is to score goals by throwing the ball into the opponent's net.
 
• It was invented in India by Mr. Raju Dabhade in 2003 and has since gained international recognition.
 
• Rollball is governed by the International Rollball Federation (IRBF) and promotes physical fitness, agility, and teamwork among players.

questions.question: Demonetisation was a new initiative taken by the Government of India in _______ to tackle the problem of corruption, black money, terrorism and circulation of fake currency in the economy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tue Nov 01 2016 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Demonetisation in India was announced on **November 8, 2016** by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• The initiative aimed to curb the widespread issues of **corruption, black money, terrorism financing, and the circulation of counterfeit currency**.
 
• The demonetisation involved the invalidation of ₹500 and ₹1000 banknotes as legal tender, which accounted for approximately **86% of the cash in circulation** at that time.
 
• New ₹500 and ₹2000 banknotes were introduced to replace the old currency, and citizens were required to exchange or deposit the old notes in banks within a specified period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Corruption**

 
 
• Corruption is the abuse of entrusted power for private gain. It can be classified as grand, petty, and political, depending on the amounts of money lost and the sector where it occurs.
 
• Corruption erodes trust, weakens democracy, hampers economic development and further exacerbates inequality, poverty, social division and the environmental crisis.
 
 
 
• **Black Money**
 
 
• Black money refers to funds earned on the black market, on which income and other taxes have not been paid. It is typically received in cash from underground economic activity and, as such, is not taxed.
 
• Black money is often used in illegal activities, such as crime, drug trade, terrorism, and corruption.
 
 
 
• **Terrorism Financing**
 
 
• Terrorism financing involves the solicitation, collection or provision of funds with the intention that they may be used to support terrorist acts or organizations.
 
• It is often done through a variety of methods, including money laundering, smuggling, and the exploitation of legitimate businesses and charities.
 
 
 
• **Fake Currency**
 
 
• Counterfeit money is imitation currency produced without the legal sanction of the state or government and designed to deceive the recipient into believing that it is genuine.
 
• Counterfeiting is a criminal activity that is often linked to other forms of crime, including money laundering, drug trafficking, and terrorism.

questions.question: The famous work "Arthashastra" attributed to which ancient Indian scholar and strategist?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chanakya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chanakya** was an ancient Indian teacher, philosopher, economist, jurist, and royal advisor.
 
• He is traditionally identified as **Kautilya** or **Vishnugupta**, who authored the ancient Indian political treatise called the **Arthashastra**.
 
• The **Arthashastra** is an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy, written in Sanskrit.
 
• Chanakya played a significant role in the establishment of the **Maurya Empire** by guiding its first emperor, Chandragupta Maurya.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Valmiki:**

 
 
• Valmiki is celebrated as the harbinger-poet in Sanskrit literature.
 
• He is the author of the epic, the Ramayana, which consists of 24,000 shlokas and seven cantos (kandas) including the Uttarakanda.
 
 
 
• **Panini:**
 
 
• Panini was an ancient Indian Sanskrit grammarian from Pushkalavati, Gandhara.
 
• He is known for his work on Sanskrit grammar, particularly his text *Ashtadhyayi* which means "Eight Chapters".
 
 
 
• **Kalidasa:**
 
 
• Kalidasa is considered the greatest poet and dramatist in the Sanskrit language.
 
• His notable works include plays like Shakuntala, Malavikagnimitram, and poems like Meghaduta and Raghuvamsha.
 
 
 
• **Arthashastra:**
 
 
• The Arthashastra is an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.
 
• It is attributed to Chanakya (also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta), who was a teacher at Takshashila University and the prime minister of the first Maurya Emperor Chandragupta.
 
• The text is divided into 15 books, which cover various aspects of governance, economics, military strategy, and other topics.

questions.question: Which sport is played by the Indian sportsperson Jwala Gutta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Badminton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jwala Gutta is a renowned Indian badminton player known for her performance in both women's and mixed doubles categories.
 
• She has represented India in multiple international competitions, including the Olympics and World Championships.
 
• Jwala Gutta has won numerous national and international titles, making her one of India's most successful badminton players.
 
• She has also been honored with the prestigious Arjuna Award, which recognizes outstanding achievement in national sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Badminton:**

 
 
• Badminton is a racquet sport played using racquets to hit a shuttlecock across a net.
 
• It is played as a singles (one player per side) or doubles (two players per side) game.
 
• Badminton is a popular sport worldwide and is known for its fast-paced gameplay and agility.
 
• Major tournaments include the All England Open, the World Championships, and the Olympics.
 
 
 
• **Arjuna Award:**
 
 
• The Arjuna Award is one of the highest honors presented by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports in India.
 
• It recognizes outstanding achievement in national sports.
 
• Recipients of the award receive a bronze statuette of Arjuna, a certificate, and a cash prize.
 
• It has been awarded annually since 1961 to recognize excellence in sports.
